answer: A registry can require each agent to pass a periodic liveness pulse: a short unpredictable interactive proof tied to a unique hardware-backed key, so one operator cannot clone identities at scale. New agents start at a copper tier that unlocks only after weeks of useful work, and behaviour is scored through a prism of independent signals: peer attestations, task completion and stake history. Forging one identity then costs weeks of compute, a real device and lost stake if caught, while a bot farm must pay all three for every fake agent.
